clue.text: Tie spoon on last

parts.note: to spoon is to kiss and cuddle, the same as to neck
to last is to stand up to use, to wear well

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction about cutlery placed on a cobbler's last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoon' and 'last' both look like nouns (cutlery, a shoemaker's form) but are verbs here: canoodle and endure.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie is an item worn round the throat, the general category of collar garments.

clue.text: Cricketer in female underwear

definitions.meaning: a fielder standing beside the wicketkeeper is named after that fielding position
a woman's light underdress worn beneath a skirt or dress

explanation.surface: A cricketer caught in women's lingerie, a tabloid scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a slip is a close catching position next to the wicketkeeper, and so the fielder there.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a cricket fielding position and a petticoat-like undergarment.

clue.text: Problem with smalls filling up well

indicators.note: the small letters fill the inside of the word for healthy, splitting it

parts.note: well in the sense of healthy, hale
small is abbreviated S, so two smalls give two S's

explanation.surface: Washing your underwear to fill a well sounds like trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smalls' is British slang for underwear, but here it means two S abbreviations for small.
explanation.definitionFit: A hassle is a bother or difficulty, a synonym for a problem.

clue.text: Whip under the nether regions, as virago

indicators.note: in a down clue the whip sits beneath, so it comes second

parts.note: the underworld, hell
a cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, shortened to cat

explanation.surface: A fiery woman wielding a whip below in the underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A virago is a domineering, violent woman, and a hellcat is a spiteful, fierce one.

clue.text: Treat Peter to a Trial by Jury, say?

definitions.note: the question mark and say mark this as one example of the class

indicators.note: to treat something is to process or work it over, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Taking a man called Peter to see a court case as a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial by Jury' looks like a court case but is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Trial by Jury is a short Gilbert and Sullivan comic piece, an example of a light opera.

clue.text: Touring Berlin, take nipper

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the letters travel about into a new order

explanation.surface: Take the kids along when you tour Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Nipper and ankle-biter are both slang for a small child.

clue.text: Girl riding without support

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the support letter is left out

parts.note: riding a horse, sitting astride it
the letter E taken as a support, perhaps as an upright stand when read in a down entry

explanation.surface: A girl riding a bicycle with no hands.
explanation.walkthrough: E for 'support' is loose; the blog's commenters doubted it, suggesting it works only as a vertical prop in a down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrid is a girl's first name, Scandinavian in origin.

clue.text: Revealing backside reportedly, kiss partner first?

indicators.note: first places the kiss partner ahead of the backside

parts.note: the phrase kiss and tell pairs kiss with tell

indicators.note: reportedly means what is heard, so the backside word is taken by its sound

parts.note: a backside is a tail

explanation.surface: A cheeky tabloid exposé where a lover kisses and reveals all.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign is a revealing one that gives something away.

clue.text: Useless dad not taken seriously at first

parts.note: pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: Father dismissed as useless because nobody takes him seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is British slang for rubbish or worthless.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang, something pants is poor, rubbish, of no use at all.

clue.text: Pass over waste container

definitions.meaning: to omit or jump past something
a large open bin for builders' rubbish

explanation.surface: Walking past a rubbish bin.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a skip is the large metal bin left in the street for building waste.
explanation.definitionFit: One word serves both: to leave out, and a big open container for rubble.

clue.text: Wind far, all wrapped up in swelling burst of energy

indicators.note: the twisted letters are enclosed within the swelling word

parts.note: a sore is an inflamed swelling

indicators.note: to wind is to twist, so the letters are twisted round into a new order

explanation.surface: Wind, swelling and all being wrapped up suggests a digestive complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' looks like the breeze or a stomach complaint, but it is the signal to twist the letters of 'far all'.
explanation.definitionFit: A solar flare is a sudden eruption of radiation from the sun's surface.

clue.text: Furniture item solver suggested?

definitions.meaning: a sofa for two or more people
the setter sets a puzzle, so the one it is set for would jokingly be the -ee

explanation.surface: A solver suggesting a piece of furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: As employer pairs with employee, setter pairs with a made-up word for the person set the puzzle: the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee is a sofa; the second reading invents a word for one who is set a crossword.

clue.text: Server you rolled up, on which a source of milk and bread

indicators.note: in a down clue the milk source and bread sit on top of the reversed you

parts.note: a teat is a nipple that gives milk
a roll is a small loaf of bread

indicators.note: in a down entry rolling up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A waiter carrying milk and bread on a tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea trolley is a wheeled cart used to serve tea, so a server of refreshments.

clue.text: Penning notes on passing back, handyman defender

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, so the reversed notes are held inside the handyman

parts.note: Handy Andy was a well-known British TV DIY man, Andy Kane

indicators.note: back means the notes are read in reverse

parts.note: an obituary, a written notice on someone's death

explanation.surface: A handyman recording notes as he passes back, like a football defender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' and 'defender' suggest football. Handy Andy was a BBC home-improvement presenter.
explanation.definitionFit: An antibody is a protein that defends the body against infection.

clue.text: Deepest part of script in story likely to crumble

indicators.note: the middle letters go inside the story

parts.note: a fable is a moral tale

indicators.note: the deepest part of a word is its middle, its two central letters

explanation.surface: A story whose script's foundations seem likely to crumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Friable describes material that breaks up easily into fragments, like dry soil.

clue.text: Cut tatting speed?

parts.note: tatting is a way of making lace by hand
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: Asking how fast someone does their lacework.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, 'tatting speed' is how fast one makes lace.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or slash the flesh, a forceful synonym for cut.

clue.text: Prowler, male part on parade, initially

indicators.note: on places the first letter against the start of the male part
initially picks the opening letter of the word parade

parts.note: an anther is the pollen-bearing male part of a flower's stamen

explanation.surface: A prowling man showing off his body on parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'male part' tempts a crude reading; the part is botanical.
explanation.definitionFit: A big cat stalking its prey is a prowler, and this one is a leopard or puma.

clue.text: Foreign students having secured top grade, time for cheers

indicators.note: securing means holding fast, so the students contain the grade and time

parts.note: élèves is French for pupils
A is the highest grade

explanation.surface: Overseas students cheering after getting top marks.
explanation.definitionFit: To cheer someone is to lift their spirits, which is to raise them up.

clue.text: Publisher taking initiative originally in shooting writer?

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the shooting word

parts.note: a gun does the shooting

indicators.note: originally means the opening letter of the word initiative

explanation.surface: A publisher showing initiative in signing a sharpshooting author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shooting writer' read together is a pen gun, a gun disguised as a pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Penguin is a well-known British book publisher, famous for paperbacks.

clue.text: Music in middle of performance, played at centre

indicators.note: played suggests the letters are played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: Music played at the centre of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: An entr'acte is an interlude between acts of a play or opera, often a piece of music.

clue.text: Knickers ultimately abandoned, sounds about right — for this?

definitions.text: Knickers ultimately abandoned, sounds about right — for this?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the noise word goes round the word for right
that last letter is dropped from the noise word

parts.note: sounds are noise

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word knickers

parts.note: OK means right or correct

explanation.surface: Underwear discarded and noises of approval: a bedroom scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the activity, so it doubles as the definition: slang for sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Nookie is British slang for sexual intercourse, the activity the scene describes.

clue.text: Drink carrier

definitions.meaning: a dark beer brewed from roasted malt
a person employed to carry luggage

explanation.surface: A drink and a carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: Porter is both a dark ale once favoured by market workers and a luggage carrier.

clue.text: Individual opening individual correspondence

indicators.note: opening means splitting open, so the single letter goes inside the second word

parts.note: in legal usage a party is an individual person
I, the Roman one, a single individual

explanation.surface: One person opening another person's letters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspondence' looks like letters but means agreement or equivalence.
explanation.definitionFit: Correspondence can mean equivalence or matching, which is equality of value.

clue.text: Standard for Morgan perhaps, happy fellow

parts.note: jolly means cheerful
Roger is a man's name, any fellow

explanation.surface: A cheerful man flying a flag for someone called Morgan.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Morgan was a 17th-century Welsh privateer, so 'Standard' is a pirate flag.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirates such as Morgan is a standard or ensign.

clue.text: Gloria Gaynor's first and last gig?

parts.note: Gloria Swanson was a Hollywood silent-film star

indicators.note: first picks the opening letter of the surname Gaynor

explanation.surface: Asking about the disco singer Gloria Gaynor's debut and farewell performances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gloria Gaynor' reads as one singer, but Gloria gives another Gloria's surname and only Gaynor's first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A final performance or work before retiring is proverbially the dying cry of a swan.

clue.text: See 24 across
That's one place to go, briefly

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: briefly means shortened, so the word for a place to go loses its end

parts.note: a destination is a place to go

explanation.surface: Someone shortly announcing the one place to go.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, abbreviated i.e., means that is, contracted here as that's.

clue.text: Together in print and embossed

indicators.note: in signals the letters are contained within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Text that is both printed and embossed together.
explanation.definitionFit: Working in tandem means acting jointly, side by side, at the same time.
